localBiteReport: The most recent available report covering Choctawhatchee Bay inshore fishing is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 — about ten days old at time of writing. According to Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (a Choctawhatchee Bay guide featured in the Northwest Florida Fishing Report), the bay is beginning to show the first signs of fall transition: large schools of baitfish (greenies/menhaden) that had been sitting in deeper open water are now pushing into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and tidal roll-downs. Redfish activity on the flats is described as improving and expected to continue building through the rest of September as the fall mullet movement gets underway — Capt. Nelson anticipates the first meaningful slot-red push arriving in the second or third week of September and running into October, with cut or butterfly-rigged finger mullet being his go-to presentation when that bite materializes. Bull redfish and jack crevalle have also been reported feeding on pogies and greenies around Rocky Bayou, Boggy Bayou, Joe's Bayou, Marler Bayou, and the East Pass area. Water temperature at this location today is 87°F, which continues to push trout and slot reds toward deeper grass edges, sandy pockets, docks, and cuts during midday — early morning and evening remain the most productive windows for flats fishing.
